title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 3
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Covers served last week and the number of seats at five cafes:

Alma: 1,840 covers, 46 seats
Bardon: 2,600 covers, 78 seats
Cleeve: 1,150 covers, 25 seats
Dray: 3,100 covers, 96 seats
Etton: 1,420 covers, 32 seats

Which cafe served the most covers per seat?
questions.explanation: Covers divided by seats: Alma 40.0, Bardon 33.3, Cleeve 46.0, Dray 32.3, Etton 44.4. Cleeve is highest at 46.0. The busiest cafe by total covers is also the largest, so it is not the hardest-working room.

questions.prompt:
Monthly online orders for a retailer:

Jan: 3,120
Feb: 3,400
Mar: 4,080
Apr: 4,590
May: 4,820

In which month was the percentage increase over the previous month greatest?
options: E. The increase was equal in each month
questions.explanation: Month-on-month: Feb +9.0%, Mar +20.0%, Apr +12.5%, May +5.0%. Mar is largest at 20.0%. April adds more orders in absolute terms than March but from a larger base, so its percentage is smaller.

questions.prompt:
Share of a company's sales by region:

North: 31%
Midlands: 24%
South West: 17%
Scotland: 13%
Wales: 9%
Other: 6%

What is the smallest number of regions that together account for more than 60% of sales?
questions.explanation: Largest first: 31 + 24 = 55%, not yet above 60. Adding South West gives 72%. So 3 regions are needed.

questions.prompt:
Seven readings, in order: 21, 21, 23, 27, 34, 41, 58

Which statement about these readings is accurate?
options: A. The mode is the smallest value and the mean is the largest of the three averages
B. The mean and the median are equal
C. The median is greater than the mean
D. The mode is greater than the median
E. All three averages are equal
questions.explanation: Mode is 21 (the repeated value), median is the fourth reading, 27, and the mean is 225/7 = 32.14. So mode < median < mean, the ordering produced by a right tail.

questions.prompt:
Two printers quote for a print run:

Printer A: GBP 180.00 setup plus GBP 0.42 a copy
Printer B: GBP 520.00 setup plus GBP 0.18 a copy

Select the run length at which the two quotes are equal AND the cheaper printer for a run of 2,000 copies.
options: A. 1,417 copies; Printer A is cheaper at 2,000
B. 1,000 copies; Printer B is cheaper at 2,000
C. 1,417 copies; Printer B is cheaper at 2,000
D. 2,000 copies; Printer A is cheaper at 2,000
E. The quotes are never equal
questions.explanation: Equal when 180 + 0.42n = 520 + 0.18n, so n = 340 / 0.24 = 1,417 copies. At 2,000: A costs GBP 1,020.00, B costs GBP 880.00, so Printer B wins above the crossover.

questions.prompt:
Covering 300 hours of work can be done in-house at GBP 26.50 an hour plus GBP 2,400.00 of fixed recruitment cost, or through an agency at GBP 41.00 an hour with no fixed cost.

Select the cheaper route for 300 hours AND the amount saved.
questions.explanation: In-house: GBP 2,400.00 + 300 × GBP 26.50 = GBP 10,350.00. Agency: 300 × GBP 41.00 = GBP 12,300.00. In-house is cheaper by GBP 1,950.00. The fixed cost is recovered because the hourly gap is GBP 14.50.

questions.prompt:
Two holdings over the same period:

Fund M: GBP 14,000.00 to GBP 17,920.00
Fund N: GBP 9,000.00 to GBP 11,970.00

Select the holding with the larger gain in money AND the holding with the larger percentage gain.
options: A. Fund M in money; Fund N in percentage
B. Fund M in money; Fund M in percentage
C. Fund N in money; Fund M in percentage
D. Fund N in money; Fund N in percentage
E. The two gained equally on both measures
questions.explanation: Money gained: Fund M GBP 3,920.00, Fund N GBP 2,970.00. Percentage gained: Fund M 28.0%, Fund N 33.0%. The larger holding gains more money; the smaller one grows faster.

questions.prompt:
A workshop has fixed costs of GBP 15,600.00 a year. Each unit sells for GBP 48.00 and costs GBP 29.00 to make.

Select the break-even volume AND the profit at 1,200 units.
questions.explanation: Contribution is GBP 19.00 a unit, so break-even is GBP 15,600.00 / GBP 19.00 = 822 units. At 1,200 units contribution totals GBP 22,800.00, less fixed costs of GBP 15,600.00, leaving GBP 7,200.00.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): spend by channel — Search GBP 4,800.00, Social GBP 9,600.00, Email GBP 1,200.00

SOURCE 2 (table): customers acquired — Search 62, Social 48, Email 90

SOURCE 3 (memo): "We should put more money into whichever channel acquires customers most cheaply."

Which channel should receive more money on the memo's own criterion?
options: D. All three are equally efficient
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Cost per acquisition: Search GBP 77.42, Social GBP 200.00, Email GBP 13.33. Email is cheapest. Email acquires the most customers in total, which Source 2 alone would suggest, but it costs far more per customer.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "Turnover grew from GBP 2,400,000.00 in 2020 to GBP 2,880,000.00 in 2025 — a 20% rise."

SOURCE 2 (note): "Prices in this sector rose 26% over the same five years."

SOURCE 3 (email): "The board wants growth measured in real terms."

Which statement is best supported for the measure the board wants?
options: A. Real turnover grew by about 20%
D. Real turnover grew by about 46%
E. Real growth cannot be calculated from these sources
questions.explanation: Nominal growth is 2,880,000/2,400,000 = 1.20. Deflating by the 1.26 price rise gives 1.20/1.26 = 0.952, about a 5% fall in real terms. Source 1 alone reports the nominal figure, and only Source 2 makes the real measure available.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): units produced — Plant 1 18,400, Plant 2 7,600, Plant 3 12,900

SOURCE 2 (table): scrap rate — Plant 1 2.3%, Plant 2 5.1%, Plant 3 3.4%

SOURCE 3 (email): "Each scrapped unit costs us the same, so target the largest number of scrapped units."

Which plant should be targeted first?
options: E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Scrapped units are output multiplied by rate: Plant 1 423, Plant 2 388, Plant 3 439. Plant 3 is highest. Plant 2 has the worst rate but the smallest output, so it is not where the most units are lost.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (memo): "Our new training raised first-year retention from 68% to 79%."

SOURCE 2 (table): retention at comparable firms that ran no new training rose from 67% to 77% over the same year.

SOURCE 3 (email): "We also raised starting salaries by 6% in the same period."

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. The training raised retention by 11 percentage points
B. The training had no effect and should be discontinued
C. Retention fell once the comparison is applied
D. The training's effect is at most about one percentage point, and the salary rise may account for part of it
E. No comparison with other firms is relevant
questions.explanation: The firm gained 11 points; comparable firms gained 10 without the training, so the difference attributable to it is about one point, and Source 3 supplies a second change that could explain some of that. Option B overstates in the opposite direction: a small effect is not a demonstrated zero.

questions.prompt:
A delivery round has 60 stops, each either a business or a residence. How many are businesses?

(1) The number of residences is four times the number of businesses.
(2) There are 48 residences.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1), b + 4b = 60, so b = 12 — sufficient. From (2), 60 − 48 = 12 — also sufficient. Each statement alone fixes the number, so the answer is D, not C.

questions.prompt:
How many people attended this year's meeting?

(1) Attendance rose by 15% on last year.
(2) Last year 320 attended and this year 368 attended.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives the change but no starting figure, so the number could be anything — insufficient. (2) states this year's attendance directly, which answers the question on its own.

questions.prompt:
What is the price of one crate?

(1) Five crates and two pallets cost GBP 214.00.
(2) Three crates and two pallets cost GBP 158.00.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: Neither alone has enough equations for two unknowns. Subtracting gives two crates = GBP 56.00, so one crate is GBP 28.00 — sufficient together.

questions.prompt:
Did more than half the members vote?

(1) 240 members voted.
(2) The club has fewer than 800 members.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives no denominator and (2) no numerator. Together, 240 out of fewer than 800 could be 240 of 300, which is more than half, or 240 of 700, which is not — so the question remains unanswered even with both.

questions.prompt:
Which hotel earns the most room revenue per room?

Hotel | Rooms | Occupancy | Annual room revenue | Staff
Ashcroft | 84 | 72% | GBP 96,000.00 | 31
Bellhaven | 120 | 64% | GBP 138,000.00 | 44
Coppice | 56 | 81% | GBP 74,000.00 | 22
Dunmore | 150 | 58% | GBP 152,000.00 | 51
Elmsworth | 72 | 77% | GBP 88,000.00 | 27
Fairholt | 98 | 69% | GBP 109,000.00 | 35
questions.explanation: Revenue divided by rooms: Ashcroft GBP 1,142.86, Bellhaven GBP 1,150.00, Coppice GBP 1,321.43, Dunmore GBP 1,013.33, Elmsworth GBP 1,222.22, Fairholt GBP 1,112.24. Coppice is highest. The hotel with the largest total revenue has the most rooms and earns less from each of them.

questions.prompt:
How many hotels have occupancy above the mean occupancy for the six?

Hotel | Rooms | Occupancy | Annual room revenue | Staff
Ashcroft | 84 | 72% | GBP 96,000.00 | 31
Bellhaven | 120 | 64% | GBP 138,000.00 | 44
Coppice | 56 | 81% | GBP 74,000.00 | 22
Dunmore | 150 | 58% | GBP 152,000.00 | 51
Elmsworth | 72 | 77% | GBP 88,000.00 | 27
Fairholt | 98 | 69% | GBP 109,000.00 | 35
questions.explanation: Mean occupancy is (72 + 64 + 81 + 58 + 77 + 69) / 6 = 70.2%. Above it: Ashcroft 72%, Coppice 81%, Elmsworth 77% — 3 hotels.

questions.prompt:
Which hotel sells the greatest number of room-nights in a year?

Hotel | Rooms | Occupancy | Annual room revenue | Staff
Ashcroft | 84 | 72% | GBP 96,000.00 | 31
Bellhaven | 120 | 64% | GBP 138,000.00 | 44
Coppice | 56 | 81% | GBP 74,000.00 | 22
Dunmore | 150 | 58% | GBP 152,000.00 | 51
Elmsworth | 72 | 77% | GBP 88,000.00 | 27
Fairholt | 98 | 69% | GBP 109,000.00 | 35
questions.explanation: Room-nights are rooms × occupancy × 365: Ashcroft 22,075, Bellhaven 28,032, Coppice 16,556, Dunmore 31,755, Elmsworth 20,236, Fairholt 24,681. Dunmore is highest — the largest hotel wins on volume despite having the lowest occupancy rate.

questions.prompt:
Which hotel ranks second highest on room revenue per member of staff?

Hotel | Rooms | Occupancy | Annual room revenue | Staff
Ashcroft | 84 | 72% | GBP 96,000.00 | 31
Bellhaven | 120 | 64% | GBP 138,000.00 | 44
Coppice | 56 | 81% | GBP 74,000.00 | 22
Dunmore | 150 | 58% | GBP 152,000.00 | 51
Elmsworth | 72 | 77% | GBP 88,000.00 | 27
Fairholt | 98 | 69% | GBP 109,000.00 | 35
questions.explanation: Revenue per staff member: Ashcroft GBP 3,096.77, Bellhaven GBP 3,136.36, Coppice GBP 3,363.64, Dunmore GBP 2,980.39, Elmsworth GBP 3,259.26, Fairholt GBP 3,114.29. Ranked highest first: Coppice, Elmsworth, Bellhaven, Fairholt, Ashcroft, Dunmore. Second is Elmsworth.
